_doc: SELECT ALL AND INHERITED LOCK — transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §13.
`actions.yaml` §select_all has always said 'Hidden and locked objects
are excluded'. It never said whether 'locked' meant the object's own
flag or its ancestry, and the two ports answered differently: jas_dioxus
`Controller::select_all` is a hand-rolled layer->child loop that checked
`child.locked()` and NEVER the layer's, so it swept up the whole contents
of a locked layer; JasSwift's `selectAll` delegates to `selectFlat`,
which skips a locked layer outright. A live prime-directive divergence,
invisible to the corpus until `jas:locked` gave a fixture a way to start
locked (§13.1).
THE DOCUMENT (locked_layer_and_element.svg):
[0]   Layer 'Locked Layer'  jas:locked
[0,0]    rect                own flag FALSE
[0,1]    group 'Inner Group' own flag FALSE
[0,1,0]    circle            own flag FALSE
[1]   Layer 'Open Layer'    unlocked
[1,0]    rect      jas:locked
[1,1]    circle              free
So the only selectable object in the document is [1,1].
GROUPLESS IN THE OPEN LAYER, and no longer for the original reason. This
case was written groupless because Select All's group-expansion difference
was UNRULED, so a group here would have gone red for a reason that is not
about lock. It is RULED now (§16, 2026-07-28: a group counts as ONE), and
the case below carries a group deliberately. This one stays groupless so
the lock vector keeps isolating the lock question.
name: select_all_skips_a_locked_layers_whole_subtree

_doc: UNGROUP ALL AND INHERITED LOCK — SCOPE-effective-locked.md Q7,
answered by DIRECT APPLICATION of §13 rather than by a new ruling.
`actions.yaml` §ungroup_all already read lock; §13 changes what the
word MEANS, so the read follows. This is NOT the unruled Q3 (whether
an operation should refuse to act on a SELECTED locked element) —
no new guard is added anywhere; an existing one now reads down the
path instead of at one node.
THE DOCUMENT (locked_inheritance.svg):
[0]   Layer 'Locked Layer'  jas:locked
[0,1]    group 'Inner Group' own flag FALSE — survives by ancestry
[1]   Layer 'Open Layer'
[1,1]    group 'Locked Group' jas:locked — survives by its own flag
[1,3]    group 'Mixed Group'  unlocked — FLATTENED
The Mixed Group is the positive control: without it this case would
be satisfied by an ungroup_all that had stopped working. Its locked
member [1,3,0] is carried out of the group unchanged — ungroup speaks
to structure, not to lock.
name: ungroup_all_leaves_a_locked_layers_groups_alone

_doc: SELECT ALL COUNTS A GROUP AS ONE, THROUGH THE ACTION SEAM —
transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §16 (D2, RULED 2026-07-28).
The twin of the operations family's headline case, one layer up: this
drives the `select_all` ACTION, which is what the Edit menu item
dispatches, rather than the `select_all` OP VERB. Both reach the same
Controller mutator, so this is not a second implementation — it is the
evidence that the seam the USER touches reaches the ruled body.
THE DOCUMENT (select_all_top_level.svg): two layers; a three-child group
'Trio' beside a solo rect in Alpha, a two-child group 'Pair' beside a
solo rect in Beta. FOUR top-level objects, so FOUR entries. Before the
ruling JasSwift produced NINE here.
name: select_all_action_counts_a_group_as_one_object
